# Best rechargeable AA batteries

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA (NiMH, 2550 mAh).** Digital Camera World's reviewer has used these for years in flash testing and reports "100 per cent reliability." They hold about 85% of their charge after a year and are rated for roughly 500 recharges. GearLab also picks them as best for high-drain gear like cameras and controllers, at about $17.99 for 4. The downsides are the price and the lower cycle life.
- Buy: the retailer links (Adorama, Amazon, Newegg, Best Buy) are in [Digital Camera World's guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries). The results didn't include a direct product URL, so check the current price there.

**Best for longevity and storage: Panasonic Eneloop (standard, 2000 mAh).** It is rated for about 2,100 recharges and keeps about 70% of its charge after 10 years. It runs shorter per charge than the Pro, but it is a good fit for remotes, clocks, and emergency kits. Retailer links are in the same [Digital Camera World guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries).

**Best budget: IKEA LADDA.** Charge-Test measured the 2450 mAh version at about 2,450 mAh at low load and about 2,350 mAh at 1A. That is very close to the Eneloop Pro. The 1900 mAh version is also close to the standard Eneloop. IKEA has never officially confirmed Panasonic makes them, though the evidence points that way, so GearLab's "same factory" claim isn't confirmed.
- Buy: [IKEA LADDA AA 1900 mAh, $9.99 for 4](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/). This is the US listing I could verify. GearLab quotes $7.99 for the 2450 mAh pack, but I couldn't confirm that on IKEA's US site, and Charge-Test's €7.99 is a European price. Check IKEA's site or your local store for the 2450 mAh version.

**Other picks from Digital Camera World:**
- **EBL 2800mAh AA** is high capacity.
- **HiQuick 2800mAh** is a value pick.
- **EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA** is for devices that need alkaline-level voltage.
- **Energizer Recharge Power Plus** is made with 15% recycled materials.

Links for these are in the [same guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries).

## Caveats
- **Amazon Basics is disputed.** GearLab recommends it for low-drain devices like clocks and remotes. Two Frame & Focal articles say it performs poorly under load and ages badly. Those articles also contain some inconsistent numbers, so I'd treat their claims with caution. I'd skip Amazon Basics for cameras, flashlights, and controllers.
- **Capacity ratings are unreliable.** Higher mAh claims on lesser-known brands are not always matched by real-world results, so the Eneloop and LADDA lines are the safer buys.

**Quick pick:** Eneloop Pro for high-drain devices, standard Eneloop or LADDA for everyday use and storage, and LADDA if you have an IKEA nearby and want to save money.
